judgment_text:
Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, to issue a Writ of Mandamus directing the respondents 1 to 3 to provide adequate police protection to conduct Sandal and Urus to the petitioner Waqf situated at No. 12/186, Big Street, Triplicane, Chennai for a period of 2 days commencing from 16.02.2026, 17.02.2026 and 18.02.2026 (27th 28th and 29th day of Shaban, eight month of Islamic Hijiri Calendar) by restraining the 5th respondent, their men, agent or whomsoever from causing any hindrance by considering the representation dated 28.01.2026.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

A.D. Jagadish Chandira, J.:— This Writ Petition has been filed for a direction, directing the respondents 1 to 3 to provide adequate police protection to conduct Sandal and Urus to the petitioner Waqf situated at No. 12/186, Big Street, Triplicane, Chennai for a period of 3 days from 16.02.2026 to 18.02.2026 (27th 28th and 29th day of Shaban, eighth month of Islamic Hijiri Calendar) by restraining the 5th respondent, their men, agent or whomsoever from causing any hindrance by considering the representation dated 28.01.2026.

2. The petitioner's Wakf is registered under Tamil Nadu Wakf Board. The appointment of Muthavalli for the petitioner's Wakf Dargah (hereinafter referred to as “Dargah”) is hereditary in nature. While so, the Tamil Nadu Wakf Board has recognized the petitioner as joint Hereditary Muthavalli for the Dargah by way of its Wakf Board Resolution dated 23.01.2024. Accordingly, the Chief Executive Officer, Tamil Nadu Wakf Board, viz., the first respondent herein, passed an order dated 16.02.2024, thereby recognizing the petitioner as the Joint Hereditary Muthavalli for the Dargah viz., Hazarath Syed Sha Murthuza Pazha Khadri & Asar-e-Shareef situated at Door No. 12/186, Big Street, Triplicane, Chennai-600 005. Thereafter, the petitioner has been managing and carrying out the day-to-day affairs of the Dargah.

3. Now, the Sandal & Urus (Kanduri) and other religious ceremonies for the Dargah are to be conducted on 16.02.2026 and the petitioner has submitted a representation before the respondents 2 to 4 seeking police protection, as the fifth respondent has challenged the petitioner's appointment as Muthavalli for the Dargah in O.A. No. 12 of 2024 before the Wakf Tribunal, seeking a declaration that the resolution passed by the Tamil Nadu Wakf Board on 23.01.2024 and the consequential order passed by the first respondent on 16.02.2024 are null and void. The fifth respondent has also sought an order of interim injunction. However, without any order of interim injunction, the matter is still pending with the Tamil Nadu Wakf Board, Chennai. Despite this, the fifth respondent has attempted to interfere with the administration and management of the petitioner as Muthavalli. The petitioner has also filed an application in O.A. No. 2 of 2025 in I.A. No. 25 of 2025 before the Tamil Nadu Wakf Tribunal, seeking injunction restraining the fifth respondent herein from disturbing the peaceful celebration of Sandal and Urus festival of the Dargah. It is also pending without any interim order.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner has no objection for the fifth respondent in participating the festival and performing worship but according to him, the fifth respondent shall not be permitted to perform any rituals.

5. The learned counsel for the first respondent submitted that as per the proceedings No. 14755/23/A9/Chennai, dated 16.02.2024 passed by the first respondent, the petitioner is appointed to function as Muthavalli and to perform the rituals during festivals.

6. The learned counsel for the fifth respondent submitted that the petitioner is the spiritual leader of the said Dargah and is responsible for the pasting of sandal and the distribution of food. Therefore, the rights of the fifth respondent cannot be prevented at any cost. The petitioner was appointed as Muthavalli and has been managing the Dargah. It would not amount that the petitioner alone can conduct Sandal and Urus or any religious spiritual functions for the Dargah. Further, the fifth respondent may be permitted to worship and conduct rituals.

7. A perusal of the records reveals that admittedly the petitioner was appointed as Muthavalli for the Dargah as per the resolution passed by the Tamil Nadu Wakf Board on 23.01.2024 and the consequential order passed by the first respondent on 16.02.2024. Though the said appointment is under challenge by the fifth respondent in O.A. No. 12 of 2024 before the Wakf Tribunal, Chennai, it is pending without any interim order. That apart, the very same Sandal and Urus (Kanduri) function was held last year and the petitioner was granted permission for police protection. Accordingly, by virtue of an order dated 26.02.2025 in W.P. No. 6700 of 2025, the petitioner had conducted the Sandal and Urus (Kanduri) festival on 27th and 27th day of February, 2025. Now, the petitioner's appointment as Muthavalli is under challenge and it is pending without any interim order. The admissions made by the petitioner cannot be countenanced. The petitioner, being Muthavalli of the Dargah, has the right to conduct the festival for the Dargah.

8. In view of the above, the fourth respondent is directed to provide adequate police protection to the petitioner for conducting Sandal and Urus (Kanduri) religious ceremony function to be held from 16.02.2026 to 18.02.2026 at Hazarath Syed Sha Murthuza Pazha Khadri & Asar-e-Shareef situated at Door No. 12/186, Big Street, Triplicane, Chennai-600 005. It is also made clear that no one can prevent the fifth respondent from participating in the festival and performing worship.

9. With the above direction and observation, this writ petition stands allowed. No costs.
